business_problem: Cambium's Marvad AI examination platform had to detect cheating and plagiarism across tens of thousands of papers, but vector-search latency reached 55 minutes and false positives surged as production volumes approached 15 million vectors.
solution_summary: Cambium used MongoDB Atlas as the data platform for Marvad AI, a national examination system that scans uploaded exam papers and flags cheating or plagiarism through vector-based similarity search. As production data volumes climbed toward tens of thousands of documents and roughly 15 million vectors, search latency ballooned to 55 minutes and false positives threatened the launch. Working with MongoDB Professional Services, Cambium tuned index sizing, memory, and search-node configuration instead of simply adding servers; the team vertically scaled to two S60 search nodes with 64 GB RAM each and reset vector-search parameters to improve precision. The result was a platform that moved from nearly an hour per query to minutes, restored real-time viability, and gave Cambium repeatable guidance for future large-vector AI projects.

data_flow: Scanned exam papers are uploaded to Marvad AI, embedded into vectors, and stored in MongoDB Atlas for similarity search. Atlas search nodes compare new submissions against the existing corpus, and tuned vector-search parameters drive the alerting workflow that flags likely cheating or plagiarism to the exam platform.
business_outcome: After tuning Atlas search nodes and vector-search settings, Cambium cut similarity-search latency from up to 55 minutes to about three minutes and got Marvad AI live in time for a national rollout.
